note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Senate race upended by Sen. Lindsey Graham's death on July 11, 2026.

SC-senate.statusNote: Special election for the seat of Sen. Lindsey Graham, who died July 11. Appointed Sen. Darline Graham defeated Rep. Ralph Norman 53 to 47 in the Aug 25 Republican runoff and is the GOP nominee. Pediatrician Annie Andrews, who won the June 9 Democratic primary with 61.5%, is the Democratic nominee. Kasie Whitener (Libertarian) and Mark Hackett (Constitution Party) are also on the November ballot.

SC-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. McMaster term-limited): Attorney General Alan Wilson (R) won the June 23 runoff with 68.6% over Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette and faces state Rep. Jermaine Johnson (D), who won the June 9 primary with 59.7%. Walid Hakim (Green) and Michael Addison (United Citizens) are also listed for the November ballot.

SC-house-1.statusNote: General election field from South Carolina's June 9, 2026 primary and June 23 runoff: Jenny Costa Honeycutt (Republican), Nancy Lacore (Democrat), Bill Reeside (Libertarian). No incumbent is on the November ballot. A certified write-in candidate, Clayton Cuteri, is not a ballot-listed candidate. We know who's running, positions not researched yet.

candidates.name: Annie Andrews
candidates.background: Pediatrician and 2022 Democratic nominee in South Carolina's 1st District, where she took 42.5% against Rep. Nancy Mace. Won the June 9 Democratic Senate primary with 61.5% over Brandon Brown, and will face the winner of the Aug 25 Republican special-primary runoff.
priorities: Affordable healthcare for every South Carolinian
Protecting voting rights and cleaning up Washington

health.label: Backs Medicaid expansion and the ACA: 'no one in the United States should go broke because they or their child got sick' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Make 'it harder for billionaires to skirt their taxes'; opposes tax breaks for billionaires, paired with PAYGO deficit rules (campaign site)

climate.label: 'The science is settled': ban offshore drilling and seismic testing off SC, transition off fossil fuels within twenty years (campaign site)

education.label: Fully fund public schools, trust teachers, no book bans (campaign site)

repro.label: Endorses the Women's Health Protection Act and 'guaranteed access to abortion services up to the point of viability' (campaign site)

democracy.label: Backs Voting Rights Act reauthorization, the Freedom to Vote Act, automatic voter registration and expanded early voting (campaign site)

candidates.name: Darline Graham
candidates.background: Appointed by Gov. McMaster to complete the term of her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, after his death on July 11; South Carolina's first female U.S. senator. Spent 28 years in state government, most recently seven years leading the SC Commission for the Blind. A first-time candidate endorsed by President Trump, she led the Aug 11 special primary with 33% and faces Rep. Ralph Norman in the Aug 25 runoff.
priorities: Kitchen-table affordability: 'the price of groceries, the price of gas, healthcare'
Employment and independence for people with disabilities
Constituent-focused service rather than foreign policy

repro.label: Advocated against abortion in her campaign ad, with no specifics on exceptions or bills yet (Forbes)

democracy.label: Backs the SAVE America Act voter ID law, echoed Trump's concerns about non-citizens voting, and would end the filibuster to pass voting legislation (Forbes)

candidates.name: Ralph Norman
candidates.background: Rock Hill real estate developer and U.S. representative for SC-05 since 2017; House Freedom Caucus member rated the most conservative House member of the 117th Congress by GovTrack. Lost the June governor's primary, then entered the Senate special primary after Lindsey Graham's death, taking 25% on Aug 11 to reach the Aug 25 runoff against Darline Graham.
priorities: Fiscal conservatism and cutting federal spending
School choice with funding following the child

climate.label: House energy page pushes 'Ending Market Distorting Subsidies, Unleashing All-of-the-Above Approach' to energy (House office)

health.label: Campaigned on strict Medicaid work requirements (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Ran on cutting federal spending for undocumented immigrants (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: 'A consistent voice for fiscal conservatism, limited government, and reduced federal spending' (Fox Carolina profile)

education.label: Supports school choice, wants 'the funding to follow the child' (Fox Carolina profile)

repro.label: Only GOP primary candidate willing to sign S. 1095, which drops exceptions for rape, incest and fatal fetal anomalies (Fox Carolina profile)

democracy.label: Voted yea on H.R. 22, the SAVE Act, requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025, 220-208 (House Clerk)

candidates.name: Alan Wilson
candidates.background: South Carolina attorney general since 2011; adopted son of U.S. Rep. Joe Wilson and a colonel in the SC Army National Guard's JAG Corps who deployed to Iraq. Won the June 23 Republican runoff with 68.6% over Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette after finishing behind her in the June 9 first round; running mate is state Sen. Mike Reichenbach.
priorities: Cut taxes and eliminate the state income tax
Law and order, backing law enforcement
Expand school choice while funding public schools

cost.label: 'Make South Carolina Affordable Again' by cutting taxes and slashing 'government red tape' (campaign site)

climate.label: As AG joined multistate suits to block EPA carbon rules for power plants, calling them 'unfounded rules' that mean 'higher power bills for South Carolinians' (SC AG office)

immigration.label: 'Deny state benefits to illegal residents, enforce immigration law'; 'If you want to be here, come here legally' (campaign site)

taxes.label: 'Fight to eliminate the state income tax', cut personal property taxes, audit government for waste (campaign site)

education.label: Backs universal school choice as a top priority: parents 'should have the same right and the same opportunity to give your kid the option' (Fox Carolina profile)

safety.label: 'Restore law and order', 'strengthen penalties for fentanyl and violent offenders'; endorsed by most GOP sheriffs for 'backing the blue' (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Firmly pro-life and will always support laws that defend the unborn' (campaign site)

democracy.label: Hailed the Supreme Court's rollback of Voting Rights Act preclearance as 'a victory for all voters' (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Joined the 20-state suit asking a federal court to declare the ACA's individual mandate unconstitutional and invalidate the entire law (SC Attorney General's office)

nullNotes.housing: checked campaign priorities page, Ballotpedia and Fox Carolina profile, nothing documented; record search also empty, only an op-ed noting he declined to join the DOJ RealPage rent price-fixing suit

controversies.label: Removed special prosecutor David Pascoe from a Statehouse corruption probe; the SC Supreme Court ruled 4-1 against him and let the investigation proceed (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Jermaine Johnson
candidates.background: State representative first elected in 2020 after defeating a 22-year incumbent; former professional basketball player who grew up working-class, earned a doctorate, and founded a nonprofit focused on job-skills training. Won the June 9 Democratic primary with 59.7% over Billy Webster and Mullins McLeod; would be South Carolina's first Black governor.
priorities: Affordability: a state minimum wage and lower property taxes for working families
Fix public education before any vouchers
Public safety: more officers plus mental-health crisis teams

cost.label: Would create a labor advisory council responsible for recommending a state minimum wage (campaign site)

health.label: Listed Medicaid expansion among his key policy priorities in his Candidate Connection survey (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Would 'fund a grant program that allows municipalities to convert existing structures into affordable housing units' (campaign site)

education.label: 'I'm not for any vouchers or anything going into private schools until we fix public education' (Fox Carolina profile)

safety.label: Mixed: would 'raise the salaries for and hire additional state and local law enforcement officers' while adding mental-health teams for 'de-escalation of crises that don't need armed police intervention' (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Medical decisions are best left to families and their doctors'; wrote a bill centering female legislators on reproductive rights (campaign site)

immigration.label: Voted nay on H.4764, which requires SC jails to join ICE's 287(g) deportation program and passed 85-30 (SC House roll call)

taxes.label: Voted nay on H.4216, the income tax overhaul cutting the bottom rate to 1.99% with a trigger path toward zero (SC House roll call)

democracy.label: Voted yea on the 2022 election law that created two weeks of in-person early voting while tightening voter ID and absentee rules (SC House roll call)
